backends._comment: default_model / default_effort are optional raw pass-through strings applied at launch. claude-kind: --model + --effort (the starting level can be changed in-session with /effort). codex: --model + --config model_reasoning_effort=<effort>. copilot: --model + --effort. Omit or empty-string default_model to add no model flag; omit or empty-string default_effort and the shared resolver falls back to high (pi and freebuff are the documented exceptions — neither launch argv carries an effort flag, and on freebuff the effort a turn runs at is server-owned). kind: freebuff also ignores default_model — its argv carries no model flag. No mat-side validation — the native CLI validates model/effort values. context_window_size caps the auto-compaction window: plain integer (250000) or k/m shorthand (350k, 1m). claude-kind exports CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW; codex adds --config model_auto_compact_token_limit. Omit to use the CLI's per-model default (200k standard / 1M extended). kind: copilot, kind: pi and kind: freebuff accept the field but no launch path reads it.

Example: selector-only gateway backend. auth_var is omitted (null) so this backend requires MAT_ANTHROPIC_GATEWAY. gateway_selector 'auto' routes through AQG's pooled failover. Allowed charset: [A-Za-z0-9_-].

Example: an enterprise/team Codex subscription through the same custom Responses provider path used by BYOK. auth_var names the opaque bearer key source; base_url is the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint. mat exports the key only as MAT_CODEX_API_KEY and writes the provider into the real role-local CODEX_HOME/config.toml.

Example: a third-party Codex provider. base_url_var is resolved from the current environment or ~/.bashrc.secret; model_catalog_json is copied as a real role-local models.json after JSON validation. Do not put an API key in config.toml.

Personal subscriptions that expose no provider key and endpoint stay on legacy credential sharing. This path may symlink auth.json/config.toml from the backend's bare canonical home; it is not an implicit fallback for an explicit provider.

Example: Copilot BYOK. auth_var/base_url_var/default_model/default_effort stay the existing launch contract; copilot_provider_type is the new protocol discriminator. Omit copilot_provider_type and mat defaults Copilot BYOK to anthropic.

Example: Copilot native login with its own GitHub token variable. No base_url_var/gateway_selector/copilot_provider_type, so this stays a native-login backend (not BYOK); auth_var here resolves as COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN and takes precedence over the global MAT_COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, letting this backend log in as a distinct GitHub identity. Must be a fine-grained PAT (github_pat_...) or `gh auth token` output (gho_...) -- a classic ghp_... PAT fails the launch.

Example: OpenCode Zen. The role home owns all XDG roots and mat renders the global role prompt at config/opencode/AGENTS.md; auth_var is required because isolated homes do not inherit OpenCode's personal auth file. context_window_size caps the model's effective window via a provider model-limit override written to the role-isolated opencode.json under the default_model's <provider-id>/<model-id> pair (e.g. opencode/... or opencode-go/...).
Example: OpenCode BYOK through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Use an opencode/<model> default_model so it selects the provider config mat writes in the isolated role home.
